steps.title: Determine iPS cell genotype
steps.instruction: Identify the genotype of the human iPS cell line at the target SNV before editing.

substeps.instruction: Retrieve the genomic sequence surrounding the variant: search the gene (e.g., OPTN) in gnomAD, locate the variant ID (or a nearby variant if unavailable), follow the UCSC link, download the FASTA sequence, and save it in SnapGene Viewer.

Design genotyping primers using Primer‑BLAST with the target locus sequence: set amplicon length 500–700 bp, Tm 62 °C ± 3 °C, GC 50%–80%, and a 1‑base GC clamp. Order at least three primer pairs (10‑nmol OPC‑cartridge purified, dissolved in TE) from Eurofins Genomics and store at –20 °C, thaw before use.
Extract genomic DNA from the iPS cells with the QIAamp DNA Mini Kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol, quantify by NanoDrop at A260, and store DNA at –20 °C (up to 6 months).

Set up a 20 µL PCR for each sample using KOD One PCR Master Mix (2×): 10 µL master mix, 3 µL forward primer (0.3 µM), 3 µL reverse primer (0.3 µM), 4 µL genomic DNA (4 ng/µL, i.e., 4 ng total), and water to 20 µL. Use the OPTN_genotyping_forward/reverse primers for the OPTN p.(Asn51Thr) locus.
Run the PCR with the following program: 98 °C 30 s (initial denaturation), 35 cycles of 98 °C 10 s (denaturation) and 68 °C 5 s/kb (extension), then hold at 4 °C.
Load 1–2 µL of PCR product on a 1.5 % agarose gel containing a fluorescent stain (e.g., GelRed), run at 100 V for ~15 min, and visualize the expected band size.
Purify the amplicon with the NucleoSpin Gel and PCR Clean‑up kit (direct purification if a single band; gel extraction if multiple bands). Quantify the purified DNA by NanoDrop and store at –20 °C.
Send the purified PCR product for Sanger sequencing (use OPTN_genotyping_forward as sequencing primer; primers should be 100–600 bp from the target).
Analyze the returned FASTA sequence with NCBI BLAST to confirm the genotype. Also inspect the chromatogram waveform for overlapping peaks indicating heterozygosity.

steps.title: Design pegRNAs
steps.instruction: Create pegRNA sequences (spacer, RTT, PBS, linker, tevopreQ1) for prime editing of the target SNV.

substeps.instruction: Input the target genomic sequence into pegRNA design tools (DeepPrime, pegFinder, PE‑Designer) to obtain candidate spacer, RTT, and PBS sequences.
Select PBS/RTT pairs according to the guideline: 11‑nt PBS with ≤12‑nt RTT or 12‑nt PBS with ≥13‑nt RTT.
Use pegLIT to design a linker that avoids base‑pairing with other pegRNA domains.
Add a 5′ G or A to the spacer to enable transcription from the U6 promoter.

Order single‑stranded oligonucleotides for the spacer, 3′‑extension (PBS + RTT + linker), and tevopreQ1 (10‑nmol OPC‑cartridge purified, dissolved in TE) from Eurofins Genomics; store at –20 °C and thaw before use.
Ensure each DNA fragment (spacer, scaffold, 3′‑extension, backbone) has ≥15 bp of homology at its ends for overlap PCR or In‑Fusion cloning.

steps.title: Construct prime‑editor plasmid
steps.instruction: Assemble a prime‑editor expression vector with the EF1A promoter driving PE4max‑MLH1dn.

substeps.instruction: Amplify the EF1A promoter fragment using pLV[Exp]-EF1A>hCas9(ns):T2A:Puro as template with EF1A_forward and EF1A_reverse primers.
Amplify the backbone of pCMV‑PEmax‑P2A‑hMLH1dn using Inverse_PEmax_forward and Inverse_PEmax_reverse primers.
Prepare 20 µL PCR reactions (KOD One Master Mix 2×): 10 µL master mix, 3 µL forward primer (0.3 µM), 3 µL reverse primer (0.3 µM), 4 µL plasmid DNA (5 ng/µL, i.e., 1 ng total), water to 20 µL.
Run PCR with: 98 °C 30 s; 35 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, 68 °C 5 s/kb; hold 4 °C.
Run 1–2 µL of each PCR on a 1.5 % agarose gel (100 V, 15 min) and verify band size.
Add 5–10 U DpnI to each 20 µL PCR mix, incubate 37 °C 10 min, then 80 °C 10 min to destroy methylated template plasmid.
Purify the PCR amplicons with the NucleoSpin Gel and PCR Clean‑up kit (extensive double wash). Quantify by NanoDrop and store at –20 °C.
Set up a 5 µL In‑Fusion reaction: 1 µL In‑Fusion snap‑assembly master mix (5×), 1 µL insert (1–20 ng/µL), 1 µL linearized vector (5–20 ng/µL), 2 µL nuclease‑free water.
Incubate the In‑Fusion mix: 37 °C 15 min, then 50 °C 15 min; hold at 4 °C.

Transform 20 µL DH5α competent cells with 0.5 µL In‑Fusion mix (DNA < 2 ng per 20 µL cells), ice 2 min, heat‑shock 42 °C 30 s, ice 2 min, add 50 µL SOC, shake 37 °C 30 min, plate on LB agar + 40 µg/mL ampicillin, incubate 37 °C overnight (12–16 h).

Perform colony PCR on 6–10 colonies using EF1A_forward/reverse (10 µL reaction: 10 µL KOD master mix, 3 µL each primer, 4 µL water, 0 µL template), PCR program as above, run products on 1.5 % agarose gel to identify correct inserts.
Inoculate 2–3 positive colonies into 10 mL BD Difco 2×YT broth + 40 µg/mL ampicillin in 50 mL tubes; shake 37 °C, 120–150 rpm, 16–20 h.
Purify plasmid DNA with a Miniprep Plus kit (endotoxin‑free). Quantify; ensure ≥1 µg/µL (≈1 000 ng/µL). Store at –20 °C.
Confirm the construct by Sanger sequencing using EF1A_sequence_forward1, EF1A_sequence_forward2, and EF1A_sequence_reverse primers.

steps.title: Assemble pegRNA expression vector
steps.instruction: Build the pegRNA backbone and insert the designed pegRNA sequences.

substeps.instruction: Amplify the backbone vector (excluding spacer‑to‑linker region) with Inverse_U6‑pegRNA_forward/reverse primers; amplify each pegRNA component (Spacer_OPTN, spCas9_scaffold, 3′‑extension + Linker_OPTN) with their respective primer pairs.
Treat each PCR product with 5–10 U DpnI (37 °C 10 min, 80 °C 10 min) to remove template plasmid.

Perform overlap PCR to fuse Spacer, scaffold, and 3′‑extension + Linker: set up a 20 µL reaction (10 µL KOD master mix, 3 µL each outer primer (Spacer_OPTN_forward, 3′‑extension + Linker_OPTN_reverse), 1 µL spacer PCR, 2 µL scaffold PCR, 1 µL 3′‑extension + Linker PCR, water to 20 µL). Run the same two‑step PCR program as above.
Purify the overlap‑PCR product (expected ~170 bp) with the NucleoSpin kit.
Perform In‑Fusion cloning of the purified pegRNA insert into the linearized backbone (same 5 µL reaction as in step 3, insert:backbone molar ratio ≈2:1). Incubate 37 °C 15 min, 50 °C 15 min.
Transform DH5α as described above, plate on LB + ampicillin, incubate overnight.
Colony PCR using Spacer_OPTN_forward and 3′‑extension + Linker_OPTN_reverse to verify insertion.
Culture positive colonies in 2×YT + ampicillin, purify plasmid with Miniprep Plus, quantify, and store at –20 °C.
Confirm pegRNA sequence by Sanger sequencing with pegRNA_sequence_forward (targets the U6 promoter).

steps.title: Test pegRNA efficiency in HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Perform a pilot prime‑editing experiment in HEK293T cells to rank pegRNAs before iPSC work.

substeps.instruction: Maintain HEK293T cells in DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin; use 2 mL medium per well of a 6‑well plate; incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; keep confluency 70–90 % (2 × 10⁵–5 × 10⁵ cells/cm²).

When 70–90 % confluent, wash with 1 mL DPBS per well, add 1 mL 0.05 % trypsin/EDTA, incubate 37 °C 2–3 min, neutralize with 2 mL DMEM + 10 % FBS, collect, spin 200 × g 3 min, resuspend, and seed 1:100–1:50 dilution.
Seed 2.0 × 10⁴ cells per well in a 48‑well plate (day 0).
Prepare transfection mix per well: 125 ng pegRNA plasmid + 125 ng PEmax plasmid in 15 µL DMEM; 0.75 µL PolyJet in 15 µL DMEM; combine (30 µL total), incubate 20–25 °C 10 min (do not exceed 20 min).
Add the 30 µL DNA‑PolyJet mixture to each well (day 0).
At 24 h post‑transfection (day 1), replace medium with DMEM + 10 % FBS containing 5 µg/mL puromycin; change medium daily.
At day 4, switch to puromycin‑free medium; continue culture.
Extract genomic DNA (as in step 1), PCR the target locus, and Sanger‑sequence.
Upload control and edited trace files to ICE (https://ice.synthego.com) to estimate editing efficiency from discordance plots.

steps.title: Transfect iPS cells with prime editor
steps.instruction: Introduce pegRNA and PEmax vectors into human iPS cells and select transfected cells.

substeps.instruction: Maintain iPS cells (line 201B7) on plates coated with 0.5 µg/cm² iMatrix‑511 in StemFit medium + 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin; use 1 mL medium per well of a 12‑well plate; incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; keep confluency 60–80 % (5 × 10⁵–1 × 10⁶ cells/cm²).

When 60–80 % confluent, wash with 1 mL DPBS, add 500 µL TrypLE Select, incubate 37 °C 6–9 min until cells round up, neutralize with 1 mL StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632, collect, spin 200 × g 3 min, resuspend in StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632, and seed 8.5 × 10²–3.5 × 10³ cells/cm². Change to Y‑27632‑free StemFit next day.
For transfection, collect 1 × 10⁵ cells, pellet (200 × g 3 min), and resuspend in 10 µL DMEM.

Add 100 ng pegRNA plasmid + 100 ng PEmax plasmid (per 1 × 10⁵ cells) to the 10 µL DMEM; add 0.8 µL PolyJet to another 10 µL DMEM; combine the two 10 µL mixes (total 20 µL) and incubate 20–25 °C 10 min.
Dilute the DNA‑PolyJet mixture 5‑fold with 20–80 µL DMEM (optimal for 201B7; determine empirically to keep >90 % viability).
Add 100 µL diluted mixture to the 1 × 10⁵ cells, gently resuspend, and incubate 37 °C 20 min.
Plate 10–20 µL of the cell suspension (≈5 × 10³–1 × 10⁴ cells) into each well of a 12‑well plate pre‑coated with 0.5 µg/cm² iMatrix‑511 containing 1 mL StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632 (day 0).
At 24 h (day 1), replace medium with StemFit + 0.25 µg/mL puromycin + 10 µM Y‑27632; change medium daily.
At day 4, switch to puromycin‑free StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632; continue changing medium every 1–2 days until colonies reach 400–600 µm diameter.

steps.title: Isolate single‑cell clones
steps.instruction: Obtain clonal iPS cell lines by limiting dilution.

substeps.instruction: Detach colonies with TrypLE Select as in step 5, prepare a single‑cell suspension at 10 cells/mL in StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632.
Seed 100 µL (≈1 cell) per well into a 96‑well plate coated with 0.5 µg/cm² iMatrix‑511 (add 200 µL medium per well to avoid meniscus effects).
Monitor wells daily; record wells that develop a single colony. If multiple colonies appear in a well, keep the well for sequencing but consider re‑dilution later.

steps.title: Expand and bank clones
steps.instruction: Grow confirmed clones, freeze cell banks, and prepare for downstream use.

substeps.instruction: Culture colonies until they reach 500 µm diameter (≈7–10 days). Re‑seed colonies into 96‑ or 48‑well plates for expansion.
When colonies are 60–80 % confluent, detach with TrypLE Select, pellet, and split:
• For banking: resuspend cell pellet in 200 µL STEM‑CELLBANKER, store at –80 °C.
• For genotyping: store pellet at –30 °C (use 1/2 to 1/20 of a 96‑well well).
Label all frozen aliquots consistently.

steps.title: Genotype clones by direct PCR
steps.instruction: Rapidly determine which clones carry the desired mutation using direct PCR from frozen pellets.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a 30 µL PCR master mix (1.1–1.2× total volume): 15 µL KOD One 2× master mix, 4.5 µL forward primer (0.3 µM, OPTN_genotyping_forward), 4.5 µL reverse primer (0.3 µM, OPTN_genotyping_reverse), 1 µL nuclease‑free water, and 5 µL cell‑derived template (see below).
Add 10 µL DPBS to each frozen cell pellet, vortex briefly, then add 1 µL of this suspension to the PCR mix; mix by inversion and spin down.
Run PCR with the same two‑step program as in step 1 (98 °C 30 s; 35 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, 68 °C 5 s/kb; hold 4 °C).
Check the ~400 bp product on a 1.5 % agarose gel; if band is weak, increase cycles to ~40 or perform a second PCR using the first product as template.
Purify the PCR product (e.g., NucleoSpin kit) and submit for Sanger sequencing (use the same primers as for step 1).
Analyze sequences to identify clones with the intended SNV.

steps.title: Expand confirmed mutant iPS clones
steps.instruction: Scale up verified mutant clones and store long‑term.

substeps.instruction: Expand each confirmed clone in iMatrix‑511‑coated plates with StemFit + 10 µM Y‑27632, then switch to Y‑27632‑free StemFit once robust growth is observed.
Prepare at least five aliquots of each clone in STEM‑CELLBANKER and store at –80 °C; for long‑term storage, transfer to liquid nitrogen.
Maintain a record linking each frozen aliquot to its sequencing result.

description: Validation of protocol Using this protocol, we introduced the missense mutation OPTN p.(Asn51Thr) into wild-type human iPS cells and obtained the desired mutant clones with an efficiency of 20%. In an independent experiment targeting the same locus, we achieved 16.7% efficiency. Furthermore, we introduced single nucleotide substitutions at two additional loci, chr9: 129,098,086 (G>A) and chr9: 129,101,921 (G>A), obtaining the desired clones with efficiencies of 2.3% and 5.3%, respectively. These results confirm the efficacy of this protocol for introducing SNVs into human iPS cells.
